title: What a shot leaves behind
target: What a bullet and a grenade actually do in R.E.P.O. after they leave your hands, so the marks on a level can be read for what they are.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A wall you do not mind marking

steps.do: Know that a bullet can carry a hurt collider, but need not.
steps.because: a bullet can carry a hurt collider and a flag for whether it has one (ItemGunBullet, hasHurtCollider, hurtCollider)

steps.do: Expect that collider to last only a moment.
steps.because: there is a timer on that hurt collider (hurtColliderTimer)

steps.do: Look at what is left where a shot landed.
steps.because: a bullet carries a hit object that it leaves where it lands (hitGameObject)

steps.do: Know that the mark is cleaned up after a time.
steps.because: the hit object has a time before it is destroyed (hitGameObjectDestroyTime)

steps.do: Expect some shots to carry extra particles.
steps.because: a bullet can carry extra particles, with a flag for whether it has them (hasExtraParticles, extraParticles)

steps.do: Read a grenade by its blink and its ticking rather than by its shape.
steps.because: the grenade blinks in a colour of its own and ticks for a set time with a tick sound (ItemGrenade, blinkColor, tickTime, soundTick)

steps.do: Stand back from the splintering as well as the blast.
steps.because: splintering has its own sound and animation curve, and the grenade raises an event when it detonates (soundSplinter, splinterAnimationCurve, onDetonate)

steps.do: Remember that a grenade can be spawned rather than thrown, and that it can show you its throw.
steps.because: it knows whether it was spawned rather than carried and it has a throw line of its own (isSpawnedGrenade, throwLine)

commonMistakes: Assuming every bullet hurts on contact.
Hunting for a mark that the game has already cleaned up.
Reading a spawned grenade as one a crewmate threw.
Standing behind cover that a grenade's splintering can still reach.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
